books.summary: Socrates is in prison awaiting execution. His friend Crito comes at dawn with an escape plan. topics: What is real, how to live

books.title: Phaedrus
books.author: Plato
books.summary: Socrates and Phaedrus walk outside Athens to a plane tree by the Ilissus, where Phaedrus reads a speech by Lysias arguing that the non-lover should be preferred to the lover. Socrates answers with two speeches of his own — and the second, the great Palinode, unfolds the soul as a winged charioteer, the immortality of the soul, and divine madness as the source of every great good. The dialogue closes with the famous critique of writing: the myth of Theuth and Thamus, and Socrates' warning that the written word is a reminder, not a teacher.
books.blurb: A walk outside the walls; rhetoric, eros, the soul as chariot.
topics: What is real, how to live

books.title: Candide
books.author: Voltaire
books.summary: Voltaire's attack on Leibnizian optimism. A young man is tutored in the belief that this is "the best of all possible worlds" — then the world systematically dismantles that belief through earthquake, war, plague, Inquisition, and the slave trade. Ends with the most famous closing line in the Enlightenment: "we must cultivate our garden."
books.blurb: A young optimist tours the worst of all possible worlds.

books.title: Oedipus Rex
books.author: Sophocles
books.summary: The king who solved the riddle of the Sphinx saves his city from plague — by discovering that the polluter is himself. Sophocles' archetypal tragedy of fate, knowledge, and the will to see what the gods have forbidden.

books.title: Oedipus at Colonus
books.author: Sophocles
books.summary: Old, blind, and exiled, Oedipus arrives at a grove outside Athens seeking the death the gods have prepared for him. Sophocles' final play, written at ninety, is a meditation on suffering, reconciliation, and the hero's strange blessing on the land that receives him.
books.blurb: The exiled king finds, at last, a place to die.
topics: The plays, in four Shakespearean modes and a Greek tradition

books.title: Antigone
books.author: Sophocles
books.summary: Two brothers have killed each other fighting for Thebes; the new ruler forbids burial to the one who attacked the city. Antigone, sister to both, buries him anyway. Sophocles' starkest confrontation between the unwritten laws of the gods and the public law of the state.
books.blurb: Bury your brother, defy the king.
topics: The plays, in four Shakespearean modes and a Greek tradition

books.author: Aristotle
books.summary: The founding text of political science. Aristotle surveys constitutions, citizenship, justice, revolution, and the best possible state — drawing on 158 real constitutions to ask what arrangement of power serves human flourishing. books.title: Leviathan
books.author: Thomas Hobbes
books.summary: Hobbes's founding work of political philosophy, written in the shadow of civil war. Without a sovereign to hold men in awe, life in the state of nature is "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short." The social contract — surrendering freedom to an absolute sovereign — is the only escape. A pitiless and enduringly controversial argument for order over liberty.
books.blurb: Without the state, life is "nasty, brutish, and short."

books.title: The Wealth of Nations
books.author: Adam Smith
books.summary: A Scottish moral philosopher writes the founding text of modern economics: the division of labor in the pin factory, the invisible hand of markets, what makes nations rich. The book that shaped two centuries of policy and still anchors the debate.
books.blurb: The invisible hand of the market, in five long books.

books.title: The Sorrows of Young Werther
books.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
books.summary: Goethe's explosive early novel of feeling: Werther falls in love with Lotte, who is promised to another man, and turns private longing into a literary event that swept Europe. A short, dangerous book about desire, self-dramatization, and the cost of making life answer to emotion.
books.blurb: A young man writes himself into love and despair.
topics: What is real, how to live

books.title: Faust, Part One
books.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
books.summary: The scholar who has mastered every science still finds himself unable to live, makes a pact with Mephistopheles, and is led through pleasure, Walpurgis-Night, and the destruction of Gretchen. The defining work of German literature — and the play that taught the modern world how to talk about ambition, knowledge, and damnation.
books.blurb: A scholar bargains his soul; results immediately complicate.
topics: The plays, in four Shakespearean modes and a Greek tradition

books.title: The Oresteia
books.author: Aeschylus
books.summary: The only surviving Greek trilogy. A king returns from Troy and is murdered by his wife. Their son returns to avenge him by killing his mother. The Furies pursue him until Athena establishes the first court of law and acquits him. Aeschylus traces the birth of justice itself out of the cycle of blood revenge.
books.blurb: A house cursed; the birth of trial by jury.
topics: The plays, in four Shakespearean modes and a Greek tradition

books.title: The Bacchae
books.author: Euripides
books.summary: Dionysus comes to Thebes in disguise, demanding that the city worship him. King Pentheus refuses. The god drives the women of Thebes into ecstatic frenzy on Mount Cithaeron, and Pentheus, fatally curious, goes up to spy. His own mother, in the grip of the god, tears him apart with her bare hands. Euripides' last play and the most disturbing in the Greek tragic canon.
books.blurb: A god comes home to a city that won't worship him.
topics: The plays, in four Shakespearean modes and a Greek tradition

books.title: Medea
books.author: Euripides
books.summary: Medea has given up everything for Jason — her father, her country, her brother — and now he is leaving her for a princess of Corinth. Her revenge will be calibrated to destroy what he loves most. The play that gave us a heroine more terrifying than any villain.
books.blurb: A wife scorned, in a foreign land, with options.
topics: The plays, in four Shakespearean modes and a Greek tradition

books.author: Augustine
books.summary: The first great spiritual autobiography. Augustine traces his journey from youthful sin through Manichaean philosophy to Christian conversion — wrestling with desire, will, and the nature of God across thirteen searingly honest books.
books.blurb: The first real autobiography — and an argument with God.
topics: Cross-shelf: scripture, devotion, and sacred poetry

books.title: Notes from Underground
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.summary: The first existentialist novel: a feverish monologue from a self-aware, spiteful man who has retreated from society to attack the rationalist faith of his age. Dostoevsky's declaration of war on "the Crystal Palace" and the seed of every novel he wrote afterward.
books.blurb: I am a sick man — a spiteful man.

books.title: Magna Carta
books.author: Anonymous (sealed by King John)
books.summary: The Great Charter of 1215 — the document that bound a king to law, sealed at Runnymede after the barons rose against royal absolutism. Its iconic Clause 39 ("No freeman shall be taken…") is the seed of due process, habeas corpus, and the rule of law in the English-speaking world.
books.blurb: The first time a king signed away some of the power.

books.title: The US Founding Documents
books.author: Various (Jefferson, Madison, et al.)
books.summary: The four texts that built the American Republic: the Declaration of Independence (1776), the Constitution (1787), the Bill of Rights (1791), and every Amendment since. Together they define how a continental democracy was imagined, codified, and then expanded to include those it once excluded.
books.blurb: Declaration, Constitution, Bill of Rights — bundled.

books.title: The Federalist Papers
books.author: Hamilton, Madison, Jay (as "Publius")
books.summary: Eighty-five newspaper essays written by Hamilton, Madison, and Jay in 1787-88 to defend the proposed Constitution. The most influential work of political theory in American history — including Madison's celebrated "factions" paper (No. 10), the "if men were angels" argument for checks and balances (No. 51), and Hamilton's case for judicial review (No. 78).
books.blurb: 85 essays defending a new constitution, published under "Publius."

books.title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass
books.author: Frederick Douglass
books.summary: Born a slave in Maryland, Frederick Douglass taught himself to read in secret, fought off the man hired to break him, and escaped north in 1838. Three years later he wrote this account — naming the masters, the plantations, and the dates — while still legally a fugitive. The most influential of the American slave narratives.
books.blurb: The most influential American slave narrative, written while its author was still legally a fugitive.

books.title: A Little Princess
books.author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
books.summary: Sara Crewe, the doted-on daughter of an English captain in India, is placed at Miss Minchin's Select Seminary in London. On her eleventh birthday her father dies and his fortune collapses; she is moved to a freezing attic and worked as an unpaid drudge. The book is the story of what survives in a person when status, money, and protection are stripped away in a single afternoon — and of the man who has been searching London for her, living next door.
books.blurb: A girl loses everything; her imagination keeps her warm.

books.title: The Jungle Book
books.author: Rudyard Kipling
books.summary: Seven stories from the Indian jungle — Mowgli raised by wolves, Rikki-Tikki-Tavi the mongoose, the White Seal, Toomai of the Elephants. Kipling's masterpiece of animal fable and moral adventure, which invented the modern coming-of-age story and shaped how the world imagines the wild.
books.blurb: A boy raised by wolves; assorted other tales.
topics: Journeys, wagers and the open sea

books.title: Around the World in Eighty Days
books.author: Jules Verne
books.summary: Phileas Fogg, the most precise man in London, bets his fortune that he can circle the globe in eighty days. From London to Bombay to Yokohama to New York — a race against time, a detective on his heels, and a rescue along the way. Verne's great comedy of English phlegm against the chaos of the world.
books.blurb: Phileas Fogg bets the club; the clock starts.
topics: Journeys, wagers and the open sea

books.summary: Written in six weeks in 1792, in furious response to a French Revolution that proclaimed the rights of man while leaving women out, and to Rousseau's Emile, which trained girls to be ornaments. Wollstonecraft argues that women are not lesser beings designed for charm and submission but rational creatures whose minds have been deliberately stunted by bad education. The founding text of feminist political philosophy.

books.title: The Adventures of Pinocchio
books.author: Carlo Collodi
books.summary: Collodi's tale of a wooden puppet carved by a poor old woodcarver, who runs away on his first day, lies, boasts, trusts every swindler on the road and keeps promising to do better. Funny, fast and often frightening, it follows Pinocchio through hunger, prison, a Field of Miracles and the belly of a shark, toward the day he stops being a puppet.

chapters.title: Come andò che Maestro Ciliegia, falegname trovò un pezzo di legno che piangeva e rideva come un bambino.
Maestro Ciliegia regala il pezzo di legno al suo amico Geppetto, il quale lo prende per fabbricarsi un burattino maraviglioso, che sappia ballare, tirar di scherma e fare i salti mortali.
Geppetto, tornato a casa, comincia subito a fabbricarsi il burattino e gli mette il nome di Pinocchio. Prime monellerie del burattino.
La storia di Pinocchio col Grillo-parlante, dove si vede come i ragazzi cattivi hanno a noja di sentirsi correggere da chi ne sa più di loro.
Pinocchio ha fame e cerca un uovo per farsi una frittata; ma sul più bello, la frittata gli vola via dalla finestra.
Pinocchio si addormenta coi piedi sul caldano, e la mattina dopo si sveglia coi piedi tutti bruciati.
Geppetto torna a casa, e dà al burattino la colazione che il pover'uomo aveva portata per sè.
Geppetto rifà i piedi a Pinocchio, e vende la propria casacca per comprargli l'Abbecedario.
Pinocchio vende l'Abbecedario per andare a vedere il teatro dei burattini.
I burattini riconoscono il loro fratello Pinocchio e gli fanno una grandissima festa; ma sul più bello esce fuori il burattinaio Mangiafoco, e Pinocchio corre pericolo di fare una brutta fine.
Mangiafoco starnutisce e perdona a Pinocchio, il quale poi difende dalla morte il suo amico Arlecchino.
Il burattinaio Mangiafoco regala cinque monete d'oro a Pinocchio perchè le porti al suo babbo Geppetto: e Pinocchio, invece, si lascia abbindolare dalla Volpe e dal Gatto e se ne va con loro.
Pinocchio, per non aver dato retta ai buoni consigli del Grillo-parlante, s'imbatte negli assassini.
Gli assassini inseguono Pinocchio; e dopo averlo raggiunto lo impiccano a un ramo della Quercia grande.
La bella Bambina dai capelli turchini fa raccogliere il burattino: lo mette a letto, e chiama tre medici per sapere se sia vivo o morto.
Pinocchio mangia lo zucchero, ma non vuol purgarsi; però quando vede i becchini che vengono a portarlo via, allora si purga. Poi dice una bugia e per gastigo gli cresce il naso.
Pinocchio ritrova la Volpe e il Gatto, e va con loro a seminare le quattro monete nel Campo dei miracoli.
Pinocchio è derubato delle sue monete d'oro, e per gastigo si busca quattro mesi di prigione.
Liberato dalla prigione, si avvia per tornare a casa della Fata; ma lungo la strada trova un serpente orribile, e poi rimane preso alla tagliuola.
Pinocchio è preso da un contadino, il quale lo costringe a far da can di guardia a un pollaio.
Pinocchio scuopre i ladri, e in ricompensa di essere stato fedele vien posto in libertà.
Pinocchio piange la morte della bella Bambina dai capelli turchini: poi trova un Colombo, che lo porta sulla riva del mare, e lì si getta nell'acqua per andare in aiuto del suo babbo Geppetto.
Pinocchio arriva all'isola delle «Api industriose» e ritrova la Fata.
Pinocchio promette alla Fata di esser buono e di studiare, perchè è stufo di fare il burattino e vuol diventare un bravo ragazzo.
Pinocchio va co' suoi compagni di scuola in riva al mare, per vedere il terribile Pesce-cane.
Gran combattimento fra Pinocchio e i suoi compagni: uno dei quali essendo rimasto ferito, Pinocchio viene arrestato dai carabinieri.
Pinocchio corre pericolo di esser fritto in padella, come un pesce.
Ritorna a casa della Fata, la quale gli promette che il giorno dopo non sarà più un burattino, ma diventerà un ragazzo. Gran colazione di caffè-e-latte per festeggiare questo grande avvenimento.
Pinocchio, invece di diventare un ragazzo, parte di nascosto col suo amico Lucignolo per il «Paese dei balocchi.»
Dopo cinque mesi di cuccagna, Pinocchio con sua gran meraviglia sente spuntarsi un bel pajo d'orecchie asinine, e diventa un ciuchino, con la coda e tutto.
A Pinocchio gli vengono gli orecchi di ciuco, e poi diventa un ciuchino vero e comincia a ragliare.

Diventato un ciuchino vero è portato a vendere, e lo compra il Direttore di una compagnia di pagliacci, per insegnargli a ballare e saltare i cerchi: ma una sera azzoppisce e allora lo ricompra un altro, per far con la sua pelle un tamburo.
Pinocchio gettato in mare, è mangiato dai pesci, e ritorna ad essere un burattino come prima: ma mentre nuota per salvarsi, è ingoiato dal terribile Pesce-cane.
Pinocchio ritrova in corpo al Pesce-cane.... chi ritrova? Leggete questo capitolo e lo saprete.
Finalmente Pinocchio cessa d'essere un burattino e diventa un ragazzo.
How Master Cherry the carpenter found a piece of wood that cried and laughed like a child.
Master Cherry gives the piece of wood to his friend Geppetto, who takes it to make himself a wonderful puppet that can dance, fence with a sword, and turn somersaults.
Back home, Geppetto starts making the puppet at once and names him Pinocchio. The puppet’s first naughty tricks.
The story of Pinocchio and the Talking Cricket, which shows how naughty children hate being corrected by those who know more than they do.
Pinocchio is hungry and finds an egg to make an omelette; but just at the best moment, the omelette flies out of the window.
Pinocchio falls asleep with his feet on the pot of coals, and next morning wakes up with his feet burned away.
Geppetto comes home and gives the puppet the breakfast the poor man had brought for himself.
Geppetto makes Pinocchio new feet and sells his own coat to buy him an ABC book.
Pinocchio sells his ABC book to go and see the puppet theatre.
The puppets recognise their brother Pinocchio and give him a wonderful welcome; but just at the best moment the puppet master Fire-Eater appears, and Pinocchio is in danger of a terrible end.
Fire-Eater sneezes and forgives Pinocchio, who then saves his friend Harlequin from death.
The puppet master Fire-Eater gives Pinocchio five gold coins to take to his dad Geppetto; but instead Pinocchio lets the Fox and the Cat trick him and goes off with them.
Having ignored the Talking Cricket’s good advice, Pinocchio runs into the murderers.
The murderers chase Pinocchio; and after catching him, they hang him from a branch of the Great Oak.
The beautiful blue-haired Girl has the puppet brought in: she puts him to bed and calls three doctors to find out whether he is alive or dead.
Pinocchio eats the sugar but will not take his medicine; when he sees the gravediggers coming to take him away, he takes it. Then he tells a lie, and his nose grows as punishment.
Pinocchio meets the Fox and the Cat again and goes with them to plant the four coins in the Field of Miracles.
Pinocchio is robbed of his gold coins, and as punishment gets four months in prison.
Freed from prison, he sets off for the Fairy’s house; but along the way he meets a horrible snake, and then gets caught in a trap.
Pinocchio is caught by a farmer, who forces him to act as watchdog for a henhouse.
Pinocchio discovers the thieves and is set free as a reward for being faithful.
Pinocchio mourns the death of the lovely Girl with the blue hair: then he meets a Pigeon who carries him to the seashore, where he jumps into the water to help his father Geppetto.
Pinocchio reaches the island of the Busy Bees and finds the Fairy again.
Pinocchio promises the Fairy to be good and to study, because he is tired of being a puppet and wants to become a good boy.
Pinocchio goes to the seashore with his schoolmates to see the terrible Shark.
A great fight breaks out between Pinocchio and his schoolmates: one of them is hurt, and Pinocchio is arrested by the police.
Pinocchio is in danger of being fried in a pan like a fish.
He returns to the Fairy’s house, and she promises that the next day he will no longer be a puppet but will become a boy. A grand breakfast of milky coffee is planned to celebrate this great event.
Instead of becoming a boy, Pinocchio secretly leaves with his friend Candlewick for the Land of Toys.
After five months of easy living, Pinocchio is amazed to find a fine pair of donkey ears growing, and becomes a little donkey, tail and all.
Pinocchio grows donkey ears, then becomes a real little donkey and starts to bray.

Now a real little donkey, he is taken to be sold, and the Director of a company of clowns buys him to teach him to dance and jump through hoops: but one evening he becomes lame, and another man buys him to make a drum from his skin.
Thrown into the sea, Pinocchio is eaten by fish and becomes a puppet again: but as he swims to safety, he is swallowed by the terrible Shark.
Inside the Shark, Pinocchio finds… who does he find? Read this chapter and you will know.
At last Pinocchio stops being a puppet and becomes a boy.
Hvordan snedkeren mester Kirsebær fandt et stykke træ, der græd og lo som et barn.
Mester Kirsebær giver træstykket til sin ven Geppetto, som tager det for at lave sig en vidunderlig dukke, der kan danse, fægte med sværd og slå saltomortaler.
Hjemme igen begynder Geppetto straks at lave dukken og giver ham navnet Pinocchio. Dukkens første narrestreger.
Historien om Pinocchio og den talende fårekylling, hvor man ser, hvordan uartige børn hader at blive rettet på af nogen, der ved mere end dem.
Pinocchio er sulten og finder et æg for at lave en omelet; men lige som det går bedst, flyver omeletten ud ad vinduet.
Pinocchio falder i søvn med fødderne på kulbækkenet og vågner næste morgen med fødderne brændt væk.
Geppetto kommer hjem og giver dukken den morgenmad, den stakkels mand havde taget med til sig selv.
Geppetto laver nye fødder til Pinocchio og sælger sin egen jakke for at købe en ABC-bog til ham.
Pinocchio sælger sin ABC-bog for at se dukketeater.
Dukkerne genkender deres bror Pinocchio og giver ham en fantastisk velkomst; men lige som det går bedst, kommer dukkeføreren Ildslugeren, og Pinocchio er i fare for at få en frygtelig ende.
Ildslugeren nyser og tilgiver Pinocchio, som derefter redder sin ven Harlekin fra døden.
Dukkeføreren Ildslugeren giver Pinocchio fem guldmønter, som han skal tage med til sin far Geppetto; men i stedet lader Pinocchio sig narre af Ræven og Katten og går med dem.
Fordi Pinocchio ikke har fulgt den talende fårekyllings gode råd, møder han morderne.
Morderne forfølger Pinocchio; og da de har fanget ham, hænger de ham fra en gren på Den Store Eg.
Den smukke Pige med det blå hår får trædukken hentet: hun lægger ham i seng og tilkalder tre læger for at finde ud af, om han er levende eller død.
Pinocchio spiser sukkeret, men vil ikke tage sin medicin; da han ser graverne komme for at hente ham, tager han den. Så fortæller han en løgn, og som straf vokser hans næse.
Pinocchio møder Ræven og Katten igen og går med dem for at plante de fire mønter på Mirakelmarken.
Pinocchio bliver bestjålet for sine guldmønter og får som straf fire måneder i fængsel.
Da han er fri af fængslet, går han mod Feens hus; men på vejen møder han en frygtelig slange og bliver derefter fanget i en fælde.
Pinocchio bliver fanget af en bonde, som tvinger ham til at være vagthund for et hønsehus.
Pinocchio opdager tyvene og bliver sat fri som belønning for sin troskab.
Pinocchio græder over den smukke Pige med det blå hår og hendes død: så møder han en Due, der bærer ham til stranden, hvor han kaster sig i vandet for at hjælpe sin far Geppetto.
Pinocchio kommer til De flittige biers ø og finder Feen igen.
Pinocchio lover Feen at være god og læse flittigt, fordi han er træt af at være en dukke og vil blive en god dreng.
Pinocchio går med sine skolekammerater ned til havet for at se den frygtelige Haj.
Et stort slagsmål bryder ud mellem Pinocchio og hans kammerater: en af dem bliver såret, og Pinocchio bliver anholdt af politiet.
Pinocchio er i fare for at blive stegt på panden som en fisk.
Han vender tilbage til Feens hus, og hun lover, at han næste dag ikke længere vil være en dukke, men vil blive en dreng. En stor morgenmad med kaffe og mælk skal fejre denne store begivenhed.
I stedet for at blive en dreng rejser Pinocchio i hemmelighed med sin ven Lysvægen til Legetøjslandet.
Efter fem måneders driverliv opdager Pinocchio til sin store overraskelse, at han får et par fine æselører, og bliver et lille æsel med hale og det hele.
Pinocchio får æselører og bliver derefter et rigtigt lille æsel og begynder at skryde.

Nu er han et rigtigt lille æsel og bliver ført hen for at blive solgt, og Direktøren for et selskab af klovne køber ham for at lære ham at danse og springe gennem ringe: men en aften bliver han halt, og en anden køber ham for at lave en tromme af hans skind.
Pinocchio bliver kastet i havet og spist af fiskene, så han bliver en dukke igen: men mens han svømmer for at redde sig, bliver han slugt af den frygtelige Haj.
Inde i Hajen finder Pinocchio … hvem finder han? Læs dette kapitel, så får I det at vide.
Endelig holder Pinocchio op med at være en dukke og bliver en dreng.
